<a id="group-program"></a>

## Programs, lines and comments

A program is plain text, one statement or more a line, separated by ":". A line may start with a number (a V2-style line number) or a label ("Start:"). Names have up to 32 letters, digits and "_", all significant, in any case; "%" at the end makes an integer, "$" a string, no suffix a float (or an integer after OPTION INTEGER).

<a id="kw-rem"></a>

### REM

`REM text   or   ' text`

A comment: the rest of the line is kept as it is and ignored. The apostrophe is the short form and may follow a statement.

```basic
REM Bird Watch, version 1
count% = 0   ' birds so far
```

Token `$8C` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [DATA](#kw-data).

<a id="kw-let"></a>

### LET

`[LET] variable = expression`

Gives a variable a value. The word LET may be left out.

```basic
LET a% = 1
name$ = "Robin"
```

Token `$84` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [CONST](#kw-const), [DIM](#kw-dim).

<a id="kw-end"></a>

### END

`END`

Ends the program: files are closed, voices silenced, and the program quits (or returns to the editor).

```basic
IF ASK("Quit now?") THEN END
```

Token `$8D` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [STOP](#kw-stop), [END IF](#kw-end-if), [END SUB](#kw-end-sub).

<a id="kw-stop"></a>

### STOP

`STOP`

Stops the program as if Ctrl+C was pressed: under the editor it breaks into the debugger at this line; CONT continues. Also the event word of ON STOP and the timer state of TIMER n STOP.

```basic
IF total% < 0 THEN STOP
```

Token `$8E` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [CONT](#kw-cont), [END](#kw-end), [ON](#kw-on).

<a id="kw-cont"></a>

### CONT

`CONT`

Continues a program stopped by STOP, Ctrl+C or a breakpoint. Used from the editor's Run menu; in a program it does nothing.

```basic
CONT
```

Token `$8F` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [STOP](#kw-stop).

<a id="kw-option"></a>

### OPTION

`OPTION INTEGER   or   OPTION MEMORY banks`

OPTION INTEGER makes names without a suffix 16-bit integers instead of floats: faster, and what new programs should start with. OPTION MEMORY gives the variables, arrays and strings that many 8 KB RAM banks (4 to 24; 4 without it).

```basic
OPTION INTEGER
OPTION MEMORY 8
```

Token `$B8` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [DEFINT](#kw-defint), [INTEGER](#kw-integer), [MEMORY](#kw-memory).

<a id="kw-integer"></a>

### INTEGER

`OPTION INTEGER`

The word of OPTION INTEGER: unsuffixed names are integers.

```basic
OPTION INTEGER
```

Token `$B9` · word.

See also: [OPTION](#kw-option), [DEFINT](#kw-defint).

<a id="kw-memory"></a>

### MEMORY

`OPTION MEMORY banks`

The word of OPTION MEMORY: how many RAM banks the variables, arrays and strings get.

```basic
OPTION MEMORY 12
```

Token `$BA` · word.

See also: [OPTION](#kw-option), [FRE](#kw-fre).

<a id="kw-defint"></a>

### DEFINT

`DEFINT letter[-letter] [, ...]`

Names without a suffix whose first letter is in the ranges are integers (as V2 programs from other BASICs write it). DEFINT A-Z is OPTION INTEGER.

```basic
DEFINT A-Z
DEFINT I-N, X
```

Token `$B7` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [OPTION](#kw-option).

<a id="group-console"></a>

## The console: PRINT and INPUT

PRINT and INPUT use the console, a window of 8 x 8 cards that opens on the first PRINT and scrolls. A V2 listing runs in it unchanged. With #h they use an open file instead.

<a id="kw-print"></a>

### PRINT

`PRINT [#h,] [value] [{; | ,} value] ... [; | ,]`

Writes values to the console, or to file h. ";" joins values without a gap, "," moves to the next 10-column zone; a ";" or "," at the end keeps the line open. "?" is short for PRINT.

```basic
PRINT "Hello"
PRINT "Birds:"; count%, "Time: "; TIME$
PRINT #1, name$
```

Token `$80` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `PutCards`, `ScrollRect`, `FWrite`.

See also: [INPUT](#kw-input), [TAB](#kw-tab), [SPC](#kw-spc), [OPEN](#kw-open).

<a id="kw-input"></a>

### INPUT

`INPUT [#h,] ["prompt";] variable [, variable] ...`

Reads values typed in the console (with a "?" prompt) or read from file h, separated by commas, into the variables.

```basic
INPUT "Your name"; name$
INPUT #1, x, y
```

Token `$81` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `PutCards`, `GetNextChar`, `FRead`.

See also: [LINE INPUT](#kw-line-input), [GET](#kw-get), [INPUTBOX$](#kw-inputbox-s).

<a id="kw-line-input"></a>

### LINE INPUT

`LINE INPUT [#h,] ["prompt";] string-variable`

Reads a whole line, commas and quotes included, from the console or from file h.

```basic
LINE INPUT "Note: "; note$
LINE INPUT #1, first$
```

Token `$82` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `PutCards`, `GetNextChar`, `FRead`.

See also: [INPUT](#kw-input), [EOF](#kw-eof).

<a id="kw-get"></a>

### GET

`GET string-variable   or   GET #h, string-variable, count`

Without #: the next key from the queue, "" when none (it does not wait). With #h: up to count bytes from file h.

```basic
GET k$
GET #1, block$, 128
```

Token `$83` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `GetNextChar`, `FRead`.

See also: [INKEY$](#kw-inkey-s), [PUT](#kw-put), [INPUT](#kw-input).

<a id="kw-tab"></a>

### TAB

`TAB(column)`

In PRINT: moves to the column (0 is the left edge).

```basic
PRINT "Name"; TAB(20); "Count"
```

Token `$E9` · function · overlay `core`.

See also: [SPC](#kw-spc), [PRINT](#kw-print).

<a id="kw-spc"></a>

### SPC

`SPC(count)`

In PRINT: writes count spaces.

```basic
PRINT "A"; SPC(5); "B"
```

Token `$EA` · function · overlay `core`.

See also: [TAB](#kw-tab), [PRINT](#kw-print).

<a id="group-flow"></a>

## Jumps and decisions

A line number or a label is a jump target. IF has a one-line form and a block form: THEN at the end of the line starts a block that END IF closes.

<a id="kw-goto"></a>

### GOTO

`GOTO line   or   GOTO label`

Continues at the line number or the label. The first jump to a number looks it up; later ones use the cached place.

```basic
GOTO 100
GOTO Start
```

Token `$85` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [GOSUB](#kw-gosub), [ON](#kw-on), [IF](#kw-if).

<a id="kw-gosub"></a>

### GOSUB

`GOSUB line   or   GOSUB label`

Calls the lines at the target as a subroutine; RETURN comes back to the statement after the GOSUB. New programs use SUB instead.

```basic
GOSUB 900
GOSUB DrawBoard
```

Token `$86` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [RETURN](#kw-return), [SUB](#kw-sub), [ON](#kw-on).

<a id="kw-return"></a>

### RETURN

`RETURN   or   RETURN expression (in a FUNCTION)`

Without a value: back from a GOSUB. With one, in a FUNCTION: ends the function with that value.

```basic
RETURN
RETURN w * h
```

Token `$87` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [GOSUB](#kw-gosub), [FUNCTION](#kw-function).

<a id="kw-on"></a>

### ON

`ON n GOTO|GOSUB targets   or   ON event CALL procedure`

ON n GOTO 10, 20, 30 jumps to the n-th target (none when n is out of range). ON ERROR GOTO line, ON ERROR GOTO 0 and ON STOP are kept for V2-style programs. ON CLICK, KEY, WHEEL, CLOSE #w and QUIT bind an event to a SUB (the event model).

```basic
ON choice% GOTO 100, 200, 300
ON ERROR GOTO 900
ON CLICK CALL Clicked
ON CLOSE #1 CALL DoQuit
```

Token `$88` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [GOTO](#kw-goto), [CALL](#kw-call), [CLICK](#kw-click), [ERROR](#kw-error).

<a id="kw-if"></a>

### IF

`IF condition THEN statements [ELSE statements]   or   IF condition THEN ... [ELSEIF ...] [ELSE ...] END IF`

Runs statements when the condition is not 0. With THEN at the end of the line it starts a block that ends with END IF, with ELSEIF and ELSE parts. THEN followed by a line number jumps there.

```basic
IF x% > 10 THEN x% = 0
IF a$ = "" THEN 200 ELSE PRINT a$
IF score% > best% THEN
  best% = score%
ELSE
  PRINT "Try again"
END IF
```

Token `$90` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [THEN](#kw-then), [ELSE](#kw-else), [ELSEIF](#kw-elseif), [END IF](#kw-end-if), [SELECT CASE](#kw-select-case).

<a id="kw-then"></a>

### THEN

`IF condition THEN ...`

Separates IF's condition from what it runs. At the end of a line it starts an IF block.

```basic
IF k$ = "q" THEN END
```

Token `$91` · word.

See also: [IF](#kw-if), [ELSE](#kw-else).

<a id="kw-else"></a>

### ELSE

`IF ... THEN ... ELSE ...   or   ELSE (in an IF block)`

What IF runs when the condition is 0: on the same line in the one- line form, or the lines up to END IF in a block.

```basic
IF n% = 1 THEN PRINT "bird" ELSE PRINT "birds"
```

Token `$92` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [IF](#kw-if), [ELSEIF](#kw-elseif), [END IF](#kw-end-if).

<a id="kw-elseif"></a>

### ELSEIF

`ELSEIF condition THEN`

Inside an IF block: a further condition, tested when the ones before it were 0.

```basic
IF t < 0 THEN
  PRINT "frost"
ELSEIF t < 10 THEN
  PRINT "cold"
END IF
```

Token `$93` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [IF](#kw-if), [ELSE](#kw-else), [END IF](#kw-end-if).

<a id="kw-end-if"></a>

### END IF

`END IF`

Ends an IF block.

```basic
IF ok% THEN
  PRINT "Saved"
END IF
```

Token `$94` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [IF](#kw-if).

<a id="group-loops"></a>

## Loops

FOR counts; WHILE tests first, REPEAT and DO ... LOOP UNTIL test last. EXIT leaves the innermost loop of its kind. An integer FOR (FOR i% = ...) never touches the float code.

<a id="kw-for"></a>

### FOR

`FOR variable = first TO last [STEP step]`

Runs the lines up to NEXT with the variable counting from first to last (by step, 1 if none; a negative step counts down).

```basic
FOR i% = 1 TO 10
  PRINT i%
NEXT
FOR x = 1 TO 0 STEP -0.25 : PRINT x : NEXT x
```

Token `$9B` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [NEXT](#kw-next), [TO](#kw-to), [STEP](#kw-step), [EXIT FOR](#kw-exit-for).

<a id="kw-to"></a>

### TO

`FOR v = a TO b   CASE a TO b   COPY ... TO x, y`

The range word of FOR and CASE, and the target of COPY.

```basic
FOR i% = 0 TO 79 : NEXT
```

Token `$9C` · word.

See also: [FOR](#kw-for), [CASE](#kw-case), [COPY](#kw-copy).

<a id="kw-step"></a>

### STEP

`FOR v = a TO b STEP s`

The amount FOR adds to its variable each time (1 without STEP).

```basic
FOR y% = 470 TO 0 STEP -10 : NEXT
```

Token `$9D` · word.

See also: [FOR](#kw-for).

<a id="kw-next"></a>

### NEXT

`NEXT [variable [, variable] ...]`

Ends a FOR loop. With names it ends those loops, innermost first.

```basic
FOR i% = 1 TO 3 : FOR j% = 1 TO 3 : PRINT i% * j% : NEXT j%, i%
```

Token `$9E` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [FOR](#kw-for).

<a id="kw-while"></a>

### WHILE

`WHILE condition ... WEND`

Runs the lines up to WEND as long as the condition is not 0; tested before each pass.

```basic
f$ = DIR$("*.TXT")
WHILE f$ <> ""
  PRINT f$ : f$ = DIR$()
WEND
```

Token `$95` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [WEND](#kw-wend), [EXIT WHILE](#kw-exit-while), [DO](#kw-do).

<a id="kw-wend"></a>

### WEND

`WEND`

Ends a WHILE loop.

```basic
WHILE n% > 0 : n% = n% \ 2 : WEND
```

Token `$96` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [WHILE](#kw-while).

<a id="kw-repeat"></a>

### REPEAT

`REPEAT ... UNTIL condition`

Runs the lines up to UNTIL, then again while the condition is 0; at least once.

```basic
REPEAT
  k$ = INKEY$
UNTIL k$ <> ""
```

Token `$97` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [UNTIL](#kw-until), [DO](#kw-do).

<a id="kw-until"></a>

### UNTIL

`UNTIL condition   or   LOOP UNTIL condition`

Ends a REPEAT loop; also the test word of DO ... LOOP.

```basic
REPEAT : n% = n% + 1 : UNTIL n% = 10
```

Token `$98` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [REPEAT](#kw-repeat), [LOOP](#kw-loop).

<a id="kw-do"></a>

### DO

`DO [WHILE|UNTIL condition] ... LOOP [WHILE|UNTIL condition]`

A loop with its test at the top, at the bottom, or none (left with EXIT DO).

```basic
DO
  DOEVENTS
  IF INKEY$ = "q" THEN EXIT DO
LOOP
```

Token `$99` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [LOOP](#kw-loop), [EXIT DO](#kw-exit-do), [WHILE](#kw-while).

<a id="kw-loop"></a>

### LOOP

`LOOP [WHILE|UNTIL condition]`

Ends a DO loop.

```basic
DO : i% = i% + 1 : LOOP UNTIL i% = 5
```

Token `$9A` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [DO](#kw-do).

<a id="kw-exit"></a>

### EXIT

`EXIT FOR|WHILE|DO|REPEAT|SUB|FUNCTION`

The first word of the EXIT statements: each leaves the innermost block of its kind.

```basic

```

Token `$A5` · word.

See also: [EXIT FOR](#kw-exit-for), [EXIT SUB](#kw-exit-sub).

<a id="kw-exit-for"></a>

### EXIT FOR

`EXIT FOR`

Leaves the innermost FOR loop, past its NEXT.

```basic
FOR i% = 0 TO 99 : IF a%(i%) = 0 THEN EXIT FOR
NEXT
```

Token `$A6` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [FOR](#kw-for), [EXIT](#kw-exit).

<a id="kw-exit-while"></a>

### EXIT WHILE

`EXIT WHILE`

Leaves the innermost WHILE loop, past its WEND.

```basic

WEND
```

Token `$A7` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [WHILE](#kw-while), [EXIT](#kw-exit).

<a id="kw-exit-do"></a>

### EXIT DO

`EXIT DO`

Leaves the innermost DO loop, past its LOOP.


Token `$A8` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [DO](#kw-do), [EXIT](#kw-exit).

<a id="kw-exit-repeat"></a>

### EXIT REPEAT

`EXIT REPEAT`

Leaves the innermost REPEAT loop, past its UNTIL.

<a id="group-select"></a>

## Choosing: SELECT CASE

SELECT CASE compares one value with a list of cases and runs the first that matches.

<a id="kw-select"></a>

### SELECT

`SELECT CASE expression`

The first word of SELECT CASE. In an expression it is the colour number 4 (the selection colour) of PAPER.

```basic
SELECT CASE n%
END SELECT
```

Token `$9F` · word.

See also: [SELECT CASE](#kw-select-case), [PAPER](#kw-paper).

<a id="kw-select-case"></a>

### SELECT CASE

`SELECT CASE expression ... END SELECT`

Starts a choice between CASE parts: the first CASE whose list holds the value runs, or CASE ELSE when none does.

```basic
SELECT CASE k$
  CASE "a", "e", "i", "o", "u"
    PRINT "vowel"
  CASE ELSE
    PRINT "other"
END SELECT
```

Token `$A0` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [CASE](#kw-case), [CASE ELSE](#kw-case-else), [END SELECT](#kw-end-select), [IF](#kw-if).

<a id="kw-case"></a>

### CASE

`CASE value [TO value] | IS op value [, ...]`

One part of SELECT CASE: values, ranges (1 TO 5) and comparisons (IS > 9), separated by commas.

```basic
SELECT CASE n%
  CASE 1, 2 TO 5, IS > 9
    PRINT "yes"
END SELECT
```

Token `$A1` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SELECT CASE](#kw-select-case), [IS](#kw-is), [TO](#kw-to).

<a id="kw-case-else"></a>

### CASE ELSE

`CASE ELSE`

The part of SELECT CASE that runs when no CASE matched; the last.

```basic
SELECT CASE d%
  CASE 0 : PRINT "none"
  CASE ELSE : PRINT d%
END SELECT
```

Token `$A2` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SELECT CASE](#kw-select-case), [CASE](#kw-case).

<a id="kw-is"></a>

### IS

`CASE IS op value`

In CASE: compares the SELECT value with = <> < > <= or >=.

```basic
SELECT CASE t : CASE IS < 0 : PRINT "frost" : END SELECT
```

Token `$A3` · word.

See also: [CASE](#kw-case).

<a id="kw-end-select"></a>

### END SELECT

`END SELECT`

Ends a SELECT CASE.

```basic
SELECT CASE x% : CASE 1 : PRINT "one" : END SELECT
```

Token `$A4` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SELECT CASE](#kw-select-case).

<a id="group-procs"></a>

## Procedures

SUB and FUNCTION make procedures with their own parameters and local variables; they may call themselves. A SUB is called by its name and its arguments, or with CALL. Scalars are passed by value, arrays (a%()) and BYREF parameters by reference.

<a id="kw-sub"></a>

### SUB

`SUB Name[(parameter, ...)] ... END SUB`

Defines a procedure. Its parameters are local. A SUB is also what menu items, icons, timers and events call.

```basic
SUB Greet(who$)
  PRINT "Hello, "; who$
END SUB
Greet "Robin"
```

Token `$AC` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [END SUB](#kw-end-sub), [CALL](#kw-call), [FUNCTION](#kw-function), [LOCAL](#kw-local), [EXIT SUB](#kw-exit-sub).

<a id="kw-end-sub"></a>

### END SUB

`END SUB`

Ends a SUB; the call returns.

```basic
SUB Tick : WINDOW STATUS #1, "", TIME$ : END SUB
```

Token `$AD` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SUB](#kw-sub).

<a id="kw-function"></a>

### FUNCTION

`FUNCTION Name[(parameter, ...)] ... END FUNCTION`

Defines a function: a procedure with a value. Assign the value to the function's name, or give it with RETURN. The name's suffix is the value's type.

```basic
FUNCTION Area(w, h)
  Area = w * h
END FUNCTION
PRINT Area(3, 4)
```

Token `$AE` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [END FUNCTION](#kw-end-function), [RETURN](#kw-return), [SUB](#kw-sub).

<a id="kw-end-function"></a>

### END FUNCTION

`END FUNCTION`

Ends a FUNCTION; the call returns its value.

```basic
FUNCTION Twice%(n%) : Twice% = 2 * n% : END FUNCTION
```

Token `$AF` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [FUNCTION](#kw-function).

<a id="kw-exit-sub"></a>

### EXIT SUB

`EXIT SUB`

Returns from a SUB at once.

```basic
SUB Save : IF f$ = "" THEN EXIT SUB
END SUB
```

Token `$AA` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SUB](#kw-sub), [EXIT FUNCTION](#kw-exit-function).

<a id="kw-exit-function"></a>

### EXIT FUNCTION

`EXIT FUNCTION`

Returns from a FUNCTION at once with the value given so far.

```basic
FUNCTION Find%(k$) : Find% = -1 : IF k$ = "" THEN EXIT FUNCTION
END FUNCTION
```

Token `$AB` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [FUNCTION](#kw-function), [RETURN](#kw-return).

<a id="kw-call"></a>

### CALL

`CALL Name[(argument, ...)]`

Calls a SUB. The same as writing the name and its arguments; also the word that binds events and timers to a SUB.

```basic
CALL Greet("Robin")
TIMER 1, 60 CALL Tick
```

Token `$B0` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SUB](#kw-sub), [ON](#kw-on), [TIMER](#kw-timer).

<a id="kw-byref"></a>

### BYREF

`SUB Name(BYREF parameter)`

A parameter passed by reference: assigning it changes the caller's variable.

```basic
SUB Swap(BYREF a%, BYREF b%)
  LOCAL t% : t% = a% : a% = b% : b% = t%
END SUB
```

Token `$B1` · word.

See also: [SUB](#kw-sub), [FUNCTION](#kw-function).

<a id="kw-local"></a>

### LOCAL

`LOCAL name [, name] ...`

Inside a procedure: variables of its own, new at each call (so recursion works), gone at its end.

```basic
SUB Count : LOCAL i%, s$
END SUB
```

Token `$B2` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [SHARED](#kw-shared), [SUB](#kw-sub).

<a id="kw-shared"></a>

### SHARED

`SHARED name [, name] ...`

Inside a procedure: says the names are the program's globals. A name a procedure does not make LOCAL is global anyway; SHARED says so on purpose.

```basic
SUB Tick : SHARED ticks% : ticks% = ticks% + 1 : END SUB
```

Token `$B3` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [LOCAL](#kw-local).

## Data, constants and arrays

<a id="kw-data"></a>

### DATA

`DATA item [, item] ...`

Values for READ, kept as written (numbers, or text in quotes when it holds commas). In an expression (FOLDER$, PICTURE$) DATA is the number 5.

```basic
DATA 3, "Robin", "Wren", "Blue tit"
```

Token `$89` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [READ](#kw-read), [RESTORE](#kw-restore).

<a id="kw-read"></a>

### READ

`READ variable [, variable] ...`

Takes the next DATA items into the variables.

```basic
READ n% : FOR i% = 1 TO n% : READ b$ : PRINT b$ : NEXT
```

Token `$8A` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [DATA](#kw-data), [RESTORE](#kw-restore).

<a id="kw-restore"></a>

### RESTORE

`RESTORE [line | label]`

The next READ starts at the first DATA again, or at the first DATA at or after the target.

```basic
RESTORE
RESTORE Birds
```

Token `$8B` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [READ](#kw-read), [DATA](#kw-data).

<a id="kw-const"></a>

### CONST

`CONST name = value`

A name for a value that never changes; assigning it is an error.

```basic
CONST W% = 640, H% = 480
```

Token `$B4` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [LET](#kw-let).

<a id="kw-dim"></a>

### DIM

`DIM name(size [, size [, size]]) [, ...]`

Makes arrays of up to 3 dimensions, indices from 0 to size. They live in RAM banks and may be large.

```basic
DIM a%(100), grid$(10, 10)
```

Token `$B5` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [REDIM](#kw-redim), [UBOUND](#kw-ubound).

<a id="kw-redim"></a>

### REDIM

`REDIM name(size [, ...]) [, ...]`

Makes an array again with new sizes; its old values are gone.

```basic
REDIM list$(n% * 2)
```

### UBOUND

`UBOUND(array [, dimension])`

The largest index of the array's dimension (1 if none is given).

<a id="group-errors"></a>

## Errors

An error stops the program unless TRY catches it. ERR, ERR$ and ERL say what happened and where.

<a id="kw-try"></a>

### TRY

`TRY ... CATCH ... END TRY`

Runs the lines up to CATCH; an error there runs the lines from CATCH to END TRY instead of stopping the program.

```basic
TRY
  OPEN #1, "Bird list.txt", "r"
CATCH
  MSGBOX "Could not read the list: " + ERR$
END TRY
```

Token `$BB` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [CATCH](#kw-catch), [END TRY](#kw-end-try), [ERR](#kw-err), [ERROR](#kw-error).

<a id="kw-catch"></a>

### CATCH

`CATCH`

Where a TRY block continues after an error.

```basic
TRY : KILL f$ : CATCH : PRINT "Not there" : END TRY
```

Token `$BC` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [TRY](#kw-try).

<a id="kw-end-try"></a>

### END TRY

`END TRY`

Ends a TRY block.

```basic
TRY : x = 1 / y : CATCH : x = 0 : END TRY
```

Token `$BD` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [TRY](#kw-try).

<a id="kw-error"></a>

### ERROR

`ERROR number [, message]`

Raises an error. 200-255 are free for programs. Also the word of ON ERROR GOTO.

```basic
ERROR 200, "No birds"
ON ERROR GOTO 900
```

Token `$BE` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [TRY](#kw-try), [ERR](#kw-err), [ON](#kw-on).

<a id="kw-resume"></a>

### RESUME

`RESUME [NEXT | line | label]`

From an ON ERROR GOTO handler: runs the failing statement again, the one after it (NEXT), or continues at a target.

```basic
900 PRINT "Error"; ERR : RESUME NEXT
```

Token `$BF` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [ON](#kw-on), [ERROR](#kw-error).

<a id="kw-err"></a>

### ERR

`ERR`

The number of the last error.

```basic
TRY : OPEN #1, f$, "r" : CATCH : PRINT ERR : END TRY
```

Token `$EC` · function · overlay `core`.

See also: [ERR$](#kw-err-s), [ERL](#kw-erl), [ERRFILE](#kw-errfile).

<a id="kw-err-s"></a>

### ERR$

`ERR$`

The message of the last error.

```basic

```

Token `$ED` · function · overlay `core`.

See also: [ERR](#kw-err), [ERL](#kw-erl).

<a id="kw-erl"></a>

### ERL

`ERL`

The line of the last error: its line number, or the source line.

```basic

```

Token `$EE` · function · overlay `core`.

See also: [ERR](#kw-err).

<a id="kw-errfile"></a>

### ERRFILE

`ERRFILE`

The kernel's error code (its x register) of the last file or system error; 0 for other errors.

```basic

```

Token `$EF` · function · overlay `core`.

See also: [ERR](#kw-err), [OPEN](#kw-open).

<a id="group-operators"></a>

## Operators

From the highest priority: ^; unary -; * / \ MOD; + -; SHL SHR; comparisons; NOT; AND; OR XOR. AND, OR, XOR and NOT work on the bits of integers; a comparison gives -1 (true) or 0.

<a id="kw-and"></a>

### AND

`a AND b`

Both true; on integers, the bits set in both.

```basic
IF MOUSEB AND 1 THEN PRINT "left"
```

Token `$C8` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [OR](#kw-or), [XOR](#kw-xor), [NOT](#kw-not).

<a id="kw-or"></a>

### OR

`a OR b`

Either true; on integers, the bits set in either.

```basic
flags% = flags% OR 4
```

Token `$C9` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [AND](#kw-and), [XOR](#kw-xor).

<a id="kw-xor"></a>

### XOR

`a XOR b`

One true but not both; on integers, the bits that differ.

```basic
v% = v% XOR $FF
```

Token `$CA` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [AND](#kw-and), [OR](#kw-or).

<a id="kw-not"></a>

### NOT

`NOT a`

True when a is false; on integers, every bit turned over.

```basic
IF NOT done% THEN PRINT "busy"
```

Token `$CB` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [AND](#kw-and).

<a id="kw-mod"></a>

### MOD

`a MOD b`

The remainder of a divided by b.

```basic
IF n% MOD 2 = 0 THEN PRINT "even"
```

Token `$CC` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [SHL](#kw-shl).

<a id="kw-shl"></a>

### SHL

`a SHL n`

The integer a with its bits moved n places left.

```basic
hi% = b% SHL 8
```

Token `$CD` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [SHR](#kw-shr).

<a id="kw-shr"></a>

### SHR

`a SHR n`

The integer a with its bits moved n places right.

```basic

```

Token `$CE` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [SHL](#kw-shl).

<a id="kw-le"></a>

### <=

`a <= b`

True when a is less than or equal to b (numbers or strings).

```basic
IF x% <= 0 THEN x% = 0
```

Token `$CF` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [>=](#kw-ge), [<>](#kw-ne).

<a id="kw-ne"></a>

### <>

`a <> b`

True when a and b differ.

```basic
WHILE k$ <> "q" : k$ = INKEY$ : WEND
```

Token `$D0` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [<=](#kw-le), [>=](#kw-ge).

<a id="kw-ge"></a>

### >=

`a >= b`

True when a is greater than or equal to b.

```basic
IF y% >= 480 THEN y% = 479
```

Token `$D1` · operator · overlay `core`.

See also: [<=](#kw-le), [<>](#kw-ne).

<a id="group-events"></a>

## Events and the program model

A program runs its main lines, then waits for events: menu items, icons, clicks, keys, the wheel, timers. Each event calls its SUB, one at a time, to its end. The menus, the clock and the switcher keep working while BASIC runs.

<a id="kw-wait"></a>

### WAIT

`WAIT EVENTS`

Ends the main lines and waits for events. Running off the end of the main lines does the same.

```basic
WAIT EVENTS
```

Token `$C5` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `appMain`.

See also: [DOEVENTS](#kw-doevents), [ON](#kw-on), [EVENTS](#kw-events).

<a id="kw-events"></a>

### EVENTS

`WAIT EVENTS`

The word of WAIT EVENTS.

```basic
WAIT EVENTS
```

Token `$C6` · word.

See also: [WAIT](#kw-wait).

<a id="kw-doevents"></a>

### DOEVENTS

`DOEVENTS`

Inside a long loop: runs the handlers of the events waiting now, then continues.

```basic
FOR i% = 1 TO 1000 : DOEVENTS : NEXT
```

Token `$C4` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `appMain`.

See also: [WAIT](#kw-wait), [SLEEP](#kw-sleep).

<a id="kw-sleep"></a>

### SLEEP

`SLEEP frames`

Waits that many frames (1/60 s); events are handled meanwhile.

```basic

```

Token `$C7` · statement · overlay `core`.

See also: [TIMER](#kw-timer), [DOEVENTS](#kw-doevents).

<a id="kw-click"></a>

`ON CLICK CALL procedure`

```basic

```

Token `$FF $80` · word · maps to `otherPressVec`, `mouseData`.

See also: [ON](#kw-on), [MOUSEB](#kw-mouseb), [MOUSEX](#kw-mousex).

<a id="kw-key"></a>

### KEY

`ON KEY CALL procedure`

The event of a key; the handler reads KEY$, KEYCODE and KEYMODS.

```basic

```

Token `$FF $81` · word · maps to `keyVector`.

See also: [ON](#kw-on), [KEY$](#kw-key-s), [KEYCODE](#kw-keycode).

<a id="kw-wheel"></a>

### WHEEL

`WHEEL   or   ON WHEEL CALL procedure`

The wheel's movement since the last read (signed; reading clears it), and the event of a wheel turn.


Token `$FF $82` · function · overlay `core` · maps to `GetMouse`.

<a id="kw-quit"></a>

<a id="group-windows"></a>

## Windows

A program draws its own window chrome; up to 4 windows. After WINDOW USE, drawing is relative to that window's body and clipped to it.

<a id="kw-window"></a>

### WINDOW

Opens window w (1-4) at card x, y, wc cards wide and hc high, with a title and options: a tool band and a status band of n rows, a close glyph, a frame, a shadow. The second form changes it.

```basic
WINDOW #1, 10, 6, 60, 40, "Bird Watch", CLOSE, FRAME, SHADOW, STATUS 2
WINDOW TITLE #1, "Bird Watch - Garden"
WINDOW USE #1
```

Token `$FF $8E` · statement · overlay `gfx` · maps to `vr_win`, `vr_win_title`, `vr_win_status`, `clipOn`, `windowTopW`, `windowBottomW`, `WRecoverRectangle`.

<a id="group-menus"></a>

## Menus

MENU lines build the menu bar; MENU SHOW puts it up. Each ITEM names the SUB it calls.

<a id="kw-menu"></a>

### MENU

`MENU title$   or   MENU SHOW   or   MENU ENABLE menu$, item$, on`

Starts a menu of the bar (its ITEMs follow, up to END MENU or the next MENU). MENU SHOW builds and shows the bar; MENU ENABLE disables an item (0: shown in parentheses) or enables it again (1).

```basic
MENU "File" : ITEM "Open...", DoOpen, "O" : ITEM "Quit", DoQuit, "Q"
MENU SHOW
MENU ENABLE "Edit", "Cut", 0
```

Token `$FF $9C` · statement · overlay `dlg` · maps to `DoMenu`, `GotoFirstMenu`, `theme_menus`.

See also: [ITEM](#kw-item), [SHOW](#kw-show), [END MENU](#kw-end-menu), [CHECK](#kw-check).

<a id="kw-item"></a>

### ITEM

`ITEM text$ [, procedure [, key$]]`

A menu item that calls the SUB, with a keyboard shortcut (Ctrl and the key, shown at the menu's right). ITEM "-" is not an item: the next item starts a group, under a dotted line.

```basic
ITEM "About Notes", About
ITEM "Save", DoSave, "S"
```

Token `$FF $9D` · statement · overlay `dlg` · maps to `DoMenu`, `keyVector`.

See also: [MENU](#kw-menu).

<a id="kw-check"></a>

### CHECK

`CHECK item$, on`

Puts a check mark ("*") before a menu item (1) or takes it away (0).


Token `$FF $9E` · statement · overlay `dlg` · maps to `DoMenu`.

See also: [ITEM](#kw-item), [MENU](#kw-menu).

<a id="kw-end-menu"></a>

### END MENU

`END MENU`

Ends a menu's ITEM lines (optional).

```basic

```

Token `$FF $9F` · statement · overlay `dlg`.

See also: [MENU](#kw-menu).

<a id="kw-show"></a>

### SHOW

`MENU SHOW`

The word of MENU SHOW.

```basic

```

Token `$FF $A0` · word · maps to `DoMenu`.

See also: [MENU](#kw-menu).

<a id="kw-enable"></a>

`MENU ENABLE menu$, item$, on`


Plays a tune on voice v in the background: T tempo, O octave, notes C D E F G A B with # and a length, R a rest.

```basic
PLAY 0, "T120 O4 C8 E8 G4"
```

Token `$FF $DA` · statement · overlay `snd` · maps to `vr_set_irq`, `VERA:PSG`.

See also: [VOICE](#kw-voice).

<a id="group-files"></a>

## Files and folders

Files have long names (up to 63 characters, no comma); at most 3 are open. A kernel's error becomes a catchable error (50 File not found, 51 Too many files ...) with ERRFILE the kernel's code.

<a id="kw-open"></a>

### OPEN

`OPEN #h, name$, mode$`

Opens a file as handle h (1-255; 3 files open at most): mode "r" read, "w" write (a new file, or the old one replaced), "m" read and write (the file must be there). A name may hold a folder ("Lists/Birds.txt"), 64 characters in all.

```basic
OPEN #1, "Holiday photos from the lake.txt", "w"
```

Token `$FF $DB` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `FOpen`.

See also: [CLOSE](#kw-close), [PRINT](#kw-print), [INPUT](#kw-input), [EOF](#kw-eof).

<a id="kw-put"></a>

### PUT

`PUT #h, s$`

Writes the bytes of s$ to file h, nothing added.

```basic
PUT #1, CHR$(0) + CHR$(1)
```

Token `$FF $DC` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `FWrite`.

See also: [GET](#kw-get), [PRINT](#kw-print).

<a id="kw-seek"></a>

### SEEK

`SEEK #h, position`

Moves file h's position (0 is the first byte).

```basic
SEEK #1, 0
```

Token `$FF $DD` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `FSeek`.

See also: [LOC](#kw-loc), [LOF](#kw-lof).

<a id="kw-lof"></a>

### LOF

`LOF(h)`

The size of file h in bytes (up to 16 MB: a float above 32767).

```basic
PRINT LOF(1); "bytes"
```

Token `$FF $DE` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `FSize`.

See also: [LOC](#kw-loc), [EOF](#kw-eof).

<a id="kw-loc"></a>

### LOC

`LOC(h)`

The position of file h.

```basic
p = LOC(1)
```

Token `$FF $DF` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `FSeek`.

See also: [SEEK](#kw-seek), [LOF](#kw-lof).

<a id="kw-eof"></a>

### EOF

`EOF(h)`

True (-1) at the end of file h.

```basic
WHILE NOT EOF(1) : LINE INPUT #1, l$ : PRINT l$ : WEND
```

Token `$FF $E0` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `FRead`.

See also: [LINE INPUT](#kw-line-input), [LOF](#kw-lof).

<a id="kw-kill"></a>

### KILL

`KILL name$`

Deletes a file.

```basic
KILL "Old notes.txt"
```

Token `$FF $E1` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `FDelete`.

See also: [NAME](#kw-name).

<a id="kw-as"></a>

### AS

`NAME old$ AS new$`

The word of NAME ... AS.

```basic
NAME a$ AS b$
```

Token `$FF $E2` · word.

See also: [NAME](#kw-name).

<a id="kw-mkdir"></a>

### MKDIR

`MKDIR path$`

Makes a folder.

```basic
MKDIR "Birds"
```

Token `$FF $E3` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `MkDir`.

See also: [RMDIR](#kw-rmdir), [CHDIR](#kw-chdir).

<a id="kw-rmdir"></a>

### RMDIR

`RMDIR path$`

Removes an empty folder.

```basic
RMDIR "Birds"
```

Token `$FF $E4` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `RmDir`.

See also: [MKDIR](#kw-mkdir).

<a id="kw-chdir"></a>

### CHDIR

`CHDIR path$`

Makes a folder the current one.

```basic
CHDIR FOLDER$(DOCS)
```

Token `$FF $E5` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `ChDir`.

See also: [CURDIR$](#kw-curdir-s), [FOLDER$](#kw-folder-s).

<a id="kw-curdir-s"></a>

### CURDIR$

`CURDIR$`

The current folder's path.

```basic
PRINT CURDIR$
```

Token `$FF $E6` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `curDirName`.

See also: [CHDIR](#kw-chdir).

<a id="kw-dir-s"></a>

### DIR$

`DIR$(pattern$)   then   DIR$()`

The first name in the current folder matching the pattern ("*" any run, "?" any one, either case), then with DIR$() the next ones; "" when there are no more. A folder's name ends with "/".

```basic
f$ = DIR$("*.TXT") : WHILE f$ <> "" : PRINT f$ : f$ = DIR$() : WEND
```

Token `$FF $E7` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `DirOpen`, `DirNext`.

See also: [CHDIR](#kw-chdir), [KILL](#kw-kill).

<a id="kw-folder-s"></a>

### FOLDER$

`FOLDER$(DOCS | APPS | FONTS | SYSTEM | DATA)`

The path of one of the card's folders.

```basic
CHDIR FOLDER$(DOCS)
```

Token `$FF $E8` · function · overlay `file`.

See also: [CHDIR](#kw-chdir).

<a id="kw-document-s"></a>

### DOCUMENT$

`DOCUMENT$`

The document a made application was opened with (its long name), "" if none; under VeraBASIC Run always "".

```basic
IF DOCUMENT$ <> "" THEN OPEN #1, DOCUMENT$, "r"
```

Token `$FF $E9` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `dataLongName`, `longNames`.

See also: [DOCUMENTS](#kw-documents), [FILEOPEN$](#kw-fileopen-s).

<a id="kw-clipboard-s"></a>

### CLIPBOARD$

`CLIPBOARD$`

The clipboard's text (the Text Scrap, plain, 255 characters at most); a line ends with CHR$(10).

```basic
t$ = CLIPBOARD$
```

Token `$FF $EA` · function · overlay `file` · maps to `scrap_get_text`.

See also: [CLIPBOARD](#kw-clipboard).

<a id="kw-clipboard"></a>

### CLIPBOARD

`CLIPBOARD s$   or   CLIPBOARD PICTURE x1, y1, x2, y2`

Puts text on the clipboard (the Text Scrap), or a rectangle of the screen (the Photo Scrap).

```basic
CLIPBOARD "copied text"
```

Token `$FF $EB` · statement · overlay `file` · maps to `scrap_put_text`, `scrap_put_photo`.

See also: [CLIPBOARD$](#kw-clipboard-s), [PICTURE](#kw-picture).

<a id="group-time"></a>

## Time, sprites and the switcher

<a id="kw-time-s"></a>

### TIME$

`TIME$`

The time as "HH:MM:SS".

```basic
WINDOW STATUS #1, "", TIME$
```

Token `$FF $EC` · function · overlay `core` · maps to `hour`, `minutes`, `seconds`.

See also: [DATE$](#kw-date-s), [TI$](#kw-ti-s).

<a id="kw-date-s"></a>

### DATE$

`DATE$`

The date as "YYYY-MM-DD".

```basic
PRINT DATE$
```

Token `$FF $ED` · function · overlay `core` · maps to `year`, `month`, `day`.

See also: [TIME$](#kw-time-s).

<a id="kw-sprite"></a>

### SPRITE

`SPRITE n, picture$   or   SPRITE n AT x, y   or   SPRITE n ON|OFF`

Sprites 2-7 (0 is the pointer, 1 the text cursor): a 24 x 21 picture, a place, shown or hidden.

```basic
SPRITE 2, ball$ : SPRITE 2 AT 100, 100 : SPRITE 2 ON
```

Token `$FF $EE` · statement · overlay `snd` · maps to `DrawSprite`, `WPosSprite`, `EnablSprite`, `DisablSprite`.

See also: [AT](#kw-at), [PICTURE$](#kw-picture-s).

<a id="kw-at"></a>

### AT

`SPRITE n AT x, y`

The word of SPRITE ... AT.

```basic
SPRITE 3 AT x%, y%
```

Token `$FF $EF` · word.

See also: [SPRITE](#kw-sprite).

<a id="kw-aside"></a>

### ASIDE

`ASIDE`

Puts the program aside (as Alt+Tab does) and shows the dock; it continues when brought back.

```basic
ASIDE
```

Token `$FF $F0` · statement · overlay `core` · maps to `TaskCtl`.

See also: [TASKS](#kw-tasks), [STAY](#kw-stay).

<a id="kw-tasks"></a>

### TASKS

`TASKS`

How many programs are put aside.

```basic
FOR i% = 1 TO TASKS : PRINT TASK$(i%) : NEXT
```

Token `$FF $F1` · function · overlay `core` · maps to `TaskCtl`.

See also: [TASK$](#kw-task-s), [ASIDE](#kw-aside).

<a id="kw-task-s"></a>

### TASK$

`TASK$(i)`

The name of the i-th program put aside.

```basic
PRINT TASK$(1)
```

Token `$FF $F2` · function · overlay `core` · maps to `TaskCtl`.

See also: [TASKS](#kw-tasks).

<a id="group-constants"></a>

## Constants

Predefined names for numbers. They are names, not keywords: a program may not assign them, and a name of its own may not take their spelling.

<a id="kw-chrome"></a>

### CHROME

`CHROME`

The colour of bars and buttons (2).


constant, value 2.

See also: [PAPER](#kw-paper).

`YELLOW`

<a id="kw-key"></a>

### KEY_...

`KEY_LEFT, KEY_RIGHT, KEY_UP, KEY_DOWN, KEY_F1 ... (api/veranda.api)`

Key codes, as KEYCODE gives them; the names and numbers are the kernel's (api/veranda.api).

| Name | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `KEY_F1` | 1 | key code |
| `KEY_F2` | 2 | key code |
| `KEY_F3` | 3 | key code |
| `KEY_F4` | 4 | key code |
| `KEY_F5` | 5 | key code |
| `KEY_F6` | 6 | key code |
| `KEY_LEFT` | 8 | key code (BACKSPACE) |
| `KEY_TAB` | 9 | key code |
| `KEY_F7` | 14 | key code |
| `KEY_F8` | 15 | key code |
| `KEY_UP` | 16 | key code |
| `KEY_DOWN` | 17 | key code |
| `KEY_HOME` | 18 | key code |
| `KEY_CLEAR` | 19 | key code |
| `KEY_STOP` | 22 | key code |
| `KEY_ESC` | 27 | key code |
| `KEY_INSERT` | 28 | key code |
| `KEY_DELETE` | 29 | key code |
| `KEY_RIGHT` | 30 | key code |
| `KEY_PGUP` | 129 | key code (API 2) |
| `KEY_PGDN` | 130 | key code (API 2; without Ctrl: Ctrl+B is 2) |
| `KEY_END` | 131 | key code (API 2; without Ctrl: Ctrl+D is 4) |
| `KEY_F9` | 137 | key code (API 2) |
| `KEY_F10` | 138 | key code (API 2) |
| `KEY_F11` | 139 | key code (API 2) |
| `KEY_F12` | 140 | key code (API 2) |

```basic
IF KEYCODE = KEY_ESC THEN END
```



See also: [KEYCODE](#kw-keycode), [KEY](#kw-key).

<a id="kw-snd"></a>

### SND_...

`SOUND SND_ERROR ... (api/veranda.api)`

The system sounds of SOUND; the names and numbers are the kernel's (api/veranda.api).

| Name | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `SND_ERROR` | 1 | PlaySound: an error (Beep) |
| `SND_WARNING` | 2 | PlaySound: a warning or a question (a dialog box with YES and NO plays it) |
| `SND_ALARM` | 3 | PlaySound: the alarm (plays with the sounds off; nothing cuts it) |
| `SND_STARTUP` | 4 | PlaySound: the start-up chime (the first program after boot) |
| `SND_EXIT` | 5 | PlaySound: leaving Veranda (ToBASIC plays it to its end) |
| `SND_APP` | 6 | PlaySound: an application starts |
| `SND_OPEN` | 7 | PlaySound: a desk accessory opens (or a window) |
| `SND_CLOSE` | 8 | PlaySound: a desk accessory closes (or a window) |
| `SND_MENU` | 9 | PlaySound: a menu tick (only with PREFS_MENUTICK) |
| `SND_TRASH` | 10 | PlaySound: the trash emptied |

```basic
SOUND SND_WARNING
```



See also: [SOUND](#kw-sound).
